summary: Core Mission Objective & Guidance: The player's goal is to complete a 3-step scientific field campaign across real Martian terrains (like Gale Crater or Hellas Planitia) by locating, driving to, and extracting 3 subsurface water-ice, basalt, or glacial core samples using a ChemCam laser drill. A 3D vertical light pillar and directional arrow guide the player directly to each objective.   Dual-Mode Gameplay: Players can seamlessly toggle between a NASA Mission Control Console (managing life support sliders, power routing, and live space weather logs) and a 3D Surface View to drive a 6-wheeled NASA rover or walk as an Astronaut EVA suit.   Real-Time NASA ISRU & Resource Trade-Offs: Players must carefully balance a limited power grid between Kilopower nuclear generators and solar arrays. Dust storms and driving cause solar panel degradation (requiring electrostatic de-dusting pulses), while life support systems consume MOXIE oxygen, water reserves, and power—forcing careful trade-offs to keep crew radiation doses and power levels safe.   Live NASA Data & Audio: The game integrates real NASA Open API feeds (Curiosity rover imagery and DONKI space weather flare alerts) alongside a rich procedural Web Audio API sound engine that simulates rocket thrusters, motor hums, laser drilling, and sonar pings.
details: ARES-MARS COMMAND & 3D ROVER TRAINER is an immersive 3D web application that merges real NASA open data with accurate scientific engineering simulations of Martian exploration and outpost survival. It puts students and junior astronauts in the commander's seat to manage a Martian habitat, balance critical resources, and drive a NASA rover or astronaut EVA suit across an authentic global Mars terrain mapped from official NASA texture assets.
